# GLM-5.2 integration tracking and GB300 full-model performance

Updated 2026-11-01.

**Head: `edebb6b2d9e8425f164ee0365260ed99b12e0829`, 39 stack commits on
`dev@a5aa637fa5dbe2b08af7b413e32306dbc086aa01`.** The tracking branch and the development branch
are both at this head. It replaces `42779557cc` with a new revision of the recipe commit (row 39),
whose recipes now carry the formal cells' DSA flags, runtime stack and Slurm launch; rows 1–38 are
unchanged. The base includes the main-to-dev sync
[#7960](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7960). Dev has also merged the nightly sync
[#8402](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8402); the stack is not yet rebased onto it.
Among other conflict resolutions, that rebase drops the MTP-tracker hunk of row 35 (main #7768
arrives with #8402) and needs a `get_run_config` stub in row 14's test.

Status at the head (details below):
- **CPU.** Per-commit gates over all 39 commits, run at `2d7d052aee`. That commit has the head's
  code and tests; the head differs from it only in the recipes under `examples/`.
- **GPU.** A 1-node GB300 smoke at `42779557cc`, which has the head's code, passes. The GPU unit
  items, a 4-node proxy pre-gate and the 1M VPP2 parity proof ran at `2c9bd94108`, whose model code
  differs from the head only in the config-time layout check and an FE version gate that is inert
  on the measured FE 1.31.
- **Performance.** The six formal 256-GPU cells of the current recipes were measured at
  `2c9bd94108` (4K, 1M) and `2d7d052aee` (128K), through an internal runner. **Run as their README
  says, without the runner, the head's recipes reproduce all six cells: medians within 0.11%** (job
  `50951`, unprofiled; see "The recipe run"). A 128K stage ablation at `42779557cc` (job `12654`,
  unprofiled, not a formal run) reproduces the 128K trained cell within 0.06% (see "128K stage
  ablation at the previous head").
- **NSys at the head's code.** Two 64-node profiling jobs at `42779557cc` cover all six cells (96
  reports). Their last unprofiled steps are within 0.21% of the formal medians: consistency
  evidence, not a formal measurement.

Profiles are not timing qualification; the unprofiled tables (the formal cells, the recipe run and
the 128K stage ablation) are the only performance claims in this PR. Publishing the development
refs does not mark this tracking-only PR ready for merge.

Tracking branch: `buptzyb:codex/tracking/glm5-2-integration`.
Long-lived development branch: `buptzyb:codex/glm5-2-dev`.
Component links below preserve source provenance.

## Integration stack

Base: `dev@a5aa637fa5dbe2b08af7b413e32306dbc086aa01`.
Head: `edebb6b2d9e8425f164ee0365260ed99b12e0829`.
Tree: `164f7237187756c170cc7b192bf1cb6d24c58952`.
There are 39 commits above the base:
- five source-PR snapshots;
- six glue commits;
- 18 upstream candidates;
- nine local commits;
- one recipe commit.

They are not 39 independent PRs. Every commit is GPG-signed with a DCO sign-off.
Row numbers are stack positions, counted from the base.

The commits are ordered in eight layers: source-PR snapshots, glue, general fixes, DSA base, DSA
dataflow, scoring and top-k, full-iteration CUDA Graph, and recipes. The full-iteration CUDA Graph
layer (#5807 and its fixes) sits above all other code, so no lower commit depends on it.

In the last column:
- **Candidate, standalone** means the commit applies to dev `a5aa637fa5` on its own.
- **Candidate, on ...** lists what the commit needs on dev. With those commits, it applies

- **Local** commits stay in this stack for now.

### Notes on individual commits

- **Row 15.** Main #6754 (in the base through #7960) runs the synchronous LayerWise MXFP8
  parameter sync through the DDP bucket groups with `grad_data` as the receive buffer. Row 15
  keeps only the per-parameter staging into the receive slot and the equal-size tensor all-gather.
- **Rows 17 and 18.** Row 17 adapts the cuDNN DSA call sites to the FE >= 1.26 defaults: global
  sparse top-k ids (`topk_indices_global=True`) and explicit bottom-right causal offsets, passed
  from FE 1.26, the release that changed the default. CPU fakes cover both frontend generations.
  Row 18 makes cuDNN DSA deterministic on top of row 17 and carries the `+inf` top-k membership
  fix.
- **Row 22.** A layer that runs KPool selection
  ([#8287](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8287)) without tail selection does not
  certify its top-k rows as non-empty. Its CPU test needs only dev.
- **Row 23.** `TransformerConfig` checks a custom `pipeline_model_parallel_layout` at parse time,
  on every rank. With `dsa_indexer_topk_freq > 1`, it rejects a layout whose pipeline stage or
  virtual stage starts on a DSA index-sharing layer. Such a layout therefore fails at parse time,
  on CPU and on every rank, rather than at model build or the first forward, on the GPU and only
  on the ranks that own the bad chunk.
- **Row 35** also fixes the test double
  `TestThdStaticPPCommunicationShapes::test_get_tensor_shapes_uses_static_thd_width`. Its config
  lacked `pipeline_model_parallel_size`, which dev reads (main #7336, synced through #7960).
- **Row 38** covers interleaved (VPP) THD full-iteration plumbing on CPU: the schedule shape and
  layout, dynamic-CP scheduling per model chunk, the per-(chunk, microbatch) static slots, and the
  dynamic-CP certificate across VPP slots.
- **Row 39** holds the native recipes (layouts under "Native full-model recipes") and their Slurm
  and Pyxis launch. It replaces `42779557cc`, whose recipes lacked the formal cells' DSA flags,
  runtime stack and launch (see "The recipe run").

### Behaviour adapted to current dev

Each snapshot is one squash-pick of its upstream PR, adapted to the current dev, so its tree does
not equal the PR head; the upstream PRs are based on older dev. The #6741 snapshot keeps its
sequence-roll code in `mtp_sequence_roll.py`. Adaptations that change behaviour (each is recorded
in its commit message):
- #6472: dev runs TransformerBlock full recompute through the common `megatron.core.recompute`
  (main #6648). The forward-sharing checkpoint wrapper lives there, so it also wraps HybridStack
  full recompute when forward sharing is enabled.
- #6741: absolute MTP rows are used only when there is no `mtp_input_mask`, no precomputed MTP
  `decoder_input`, and the attention CP layout is not `contiguous`. In all other cases dev's
  cumulative roll runs.
- THD full-iteration graphs and main #7046's HybridEP check: the check requires
  `moe_hybridep_pad_variable_tokens` for sequence packing and exempts
  `cuda_graph_impl='full_iteration'`, whose static inputs already pad every rank to
  `max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank`.
- RNG generators are registered at capture only when dev's
  `cudagraph_needs_generator_registration()` asks for it (main #7348).
- Static-certified dynamic CP (row 36) follows dev's CP1 contract from main #7045:
  `cp_group=None` plus `cp_singleton_group`.
- The DeepGEMM scorer (row 33) needs `deep_gemm >= 2.8.1`. Dev's `batch_invariant` extra pins
  2.8.0, which falls back to the cuDNN MXFP8 scorer.

## Native full-model recipes

256 GB300, 78 decoder layers (3 dense + 75 MoE), 256 experts,
TP1/PP4/EP64/configured CP64 (1M: interleaved, two virtual stages per PP rank),
packed THD/dynamic CP, shared repeated MTP7
E2E-TV with detached heads, per-head Muon, force balance and MoK. No offload.
MXFP8 covers eligible projection/grouped GEMMs, MoK routed experts and the DSA
indexer's key scoring (DeepGEMM). MoK shared experts use BF16, with FP8 execution
and FP8 parameter storage disabled; cuDNN DSA sparse attention remains BF16, with
FP32 reductions/state where required. This is a performance
recipe, not long-term convergence or complete official optimizer-parity evidence.
Data uses NullTokenizer and fixed-length varlen mock samples with force-balanced
routing; these results do not establish real-data performance or convergence.

| Property | 4K | 128K | 1M |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Nominal sequence limit | 4,096 | 131,072 | 1,048,576 |
| Valid post-shift tokens/sample | 3,968 | 126,976 | 1,015,808 |
| Effective CP / DP | 1 / 64 | 32 / 2 | 64 / 1 |
| GBS / MBS | 2,048 / 1 | 64 / 1 | 8 / 1 |
| Realized microbatches/step | 32 | 32 | 8 |
| Local valid tokens / capacity | 3,968 / 4,096 | 3,968 / 4,096 | 15,872 / 16,384 |
| Valid global tokens/step | 8,126,464 | 8,126,464 | 8,126,464 |
| Decoder layers per PP rank + MTP7 | 22/24/24/8 + 7 | 22/24/24/8 + 7 | 22/24/20/12 + 7 (VPP2) |
| Pipeline schedule | 1F1B | 1F1B | Interleaved, batched PP send/recv |
| Recompute | Layernorm only | Layernorm only | Full uniform1 |
| MoK mini / macro | 4,096 / 40,960 | 4,096 / 40,960 | 4,096 / 131,072 |

Pipeline layouts:
- 4K and 128K: `Et*22|t*24|t*24|t*8m*7L` (1F1B). PP3 also holds MTP7 and the output head, so it
  carries the fewest decoder layers.
- 1M: `Et*10|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*8|m*7L`, interleaved with two virtual stages per PP rank
  (22/24/20/12 decoder layers per rank). It sets `no_overlap_p2p_communication`, because
  full-iteration CUDA Graphs are validated with batched PP send/recv only.
- With index sharing every fourth layer, every stage and virtual stage must start at a layer that
  computes its own top-k, so stage boundaries can only move in steps of four layers (the current
  chunks start at decoder layers 1, 23, 47 and 71, and at 1M at 1, 11, 23, 35, 47, 59 and 71).
  Row 23 enforces this at config time.

Recipes: `examples/moe_recipes/glm5_2/gb300/`
`mxfp8_THD{4K,128K,1M}_256GPU_TP1PP4EP64CP64_full_cg_mok.yaml`;
renderer: `examples/moe_recipes/glm5_2/run.py`; Slurm launch: `srun_rank.sh` and
`check_placement.py` next to it. Their README gives the runtime artifacts, the launch steps and
the validation scope (the formal cells and the recipe run).
Actual topology places each EP64 group within one of four NVL domains.
The sweep compares runnable recipes. Local tokens, CP, microbatch count, PP split, schedule and
recompute differ across lengths, not just sequence length.

## Validation of the head

**Where each check ran.** Evidence comes from five source commits; only the head is on this
branch. `42779557cc`, `97385107b0` and `2d7d052aee` share rows 1–38 with it, and `2c9bd94108` is a
stack on the same base. Tags on `buptzyb/Megatron-LM` keep the other four:
`glm5-2/42779557cc-previous-head`, `glm5-2/97385107b0-recipe-run`, `glm5-2/2d7d052aee-formal-128k`
and `glm5-2/2c9bd94108-formal-4k-1m`.
- Head: the CPU checks of its recipes (renders against the formal cells' arguments and
  environment, Megatron's argument parsing and config build of each rendered cell, and the
  README's steps against test stand-ins).
- `97385107b0`: the head's tree except for the recipe README's text, which then lacked the recipe
  run's results. The recipe run `50951` ran here.
- `42779557cc` (the previous head): the head's code, with the recipes before they carried the
  formal cells' DSA flags, runtime stack and launch. The 1-node smoke `12036`, the NSys profiles
  and the 128K stage ablation `12654` ran here.
- `2d7d052aee`: the same code and tests as the head; the head differs from it only in the recipes
  under `examples/`. The per-commit CPU gates, lint, isolation, kernel-determinism coverage, the
  rendered-cell argument checks, the 1-node smoke `12007` and the 128K formal cells ran here.
- `2c9bd94108`: differs from the head in comments, docs, tests and recipes, and in other
  code only by the config-time layout check (row 23) and the FE causal-offset gate (1.29 instead
  of 1.26), which makes no difference on the measured FE 1.31. The GPU unit items, the 4-node
  proxy pre-gate, the VPP2 parity proof, the 1-node smoke `11491` and the 4K and 1M formal cells
  ran here; the formal jobs set the current layouts at run time.

Checks:
- **Per-commit CPU gate (at `2d7d052aee`).** 238 unit-test files ran at dev `a5aa637fa5` and at
  each of the 39 commits, 40 points in all. They are every file the stack touches, plus every file
  that imports touched code. Each result was compared with dev, test id by test id.
  - At the top commit (9,325 test ids), no test that passes on dev fails.
  - Rows 1 and 4 (the #6472 and #6850 snapshots) carry known interim test-double failures in dev
    tests. Glue rows 5 and 6 fix them.
  - The 51 stack tests that fail on CPU need NCCL or a GPU.
- **Lint.** Against dev, black, isort, pylint and ruff are clean at `2d7d052aee`, as is the check
  that `megatron.core` does not import `megatron.training`. The same tools are clean on each
  commit for the files it touches, except the #6850 snapshot (row 4). Its formatting findings are
  fixed by glue row 6.
- **Recipes and arguments.**
  - The rendered 4K/128K/1M cells of the current recipes go through Megatron's argument parsing
    and config build. Each calls the config-time DSA layout check exactly once.

**What each stage changes.**
- P0–P2 ran the head plus local, experiment-only feature-disabling patches (not part of this
  stack); P3 and P4 ran the head unchanged.
  - In P0–P2, one patch reverts #6166's invalid-slot handling and turns off the inverse-permutation
    backward (row 24) and top-k certificate sharing (row 27).
  - In P0, one patch turns off the packed fused indexer scorer, so every call takes the bound-aware
    unfused per-head fallback (FP32 matmuls; BF16 indexer only). This per-head path is the
    intended P0 stage definition and the validators require it on every call; it is not an
    unintended fallback in the sense of "Metric scope and qualification limits" below.
  - In P0, one patch restores the pre-#6206 DSA layout: the packed-CP layout is built on the
    device, per rank, on every DSA call, with no host layout, memo or prebuilt tables.
  - In P1, one patch turns off only the prebuilt layout tables; the #6206 host layout is built once
    per microbatch and memoized.
  - The layout patches change timing only: in CPU tests the layout tables and the DSA forward
    inputs are bitwise identical to the head's.
- P0 and P1 are true eager (no full-iteration graph, no static dynamic CP), with HybridEP padding
  variable token counts, as eager HybridEP requires. P2–P4 run the native full-iteration graph,
  captured at step 4.
- P0–P3 use HybridEP with paged stash (rank capacity factor 1.2, GLU32 expert layout) instead of
  MoK; P4 is the native recipe.
- P1 and P2 score with the BF16 cuDNN packed fused scorer, including its `-inf` prefill. P3 adds
  #6166, rows 24 and 27, the MXFP8 indexer with the DeepGEMM scorer, and DeepSelect top-k; the
  prefill goes away with DeepGEMM, which never pre-fills (the row 28 skip is inert in every
  stage).
- The MTP optimizations, #6741 absolute-row addressing and the shard-only shared-embedding gradient
  all-reduce (row 12), are on in every stage.
- P4 runs the launch arguments of the 128K trained formal cell on the same 64 nodes as job `12015`
  and reproduces it: 15.728 / 15.720 s against 15.72805 s, 226.9 GiB max allocated in both.

**How to read it.**
- Stage gains depend on the order of the stages: each delta is measured on top of the stages before
  it.
- P0 is not a pure historical baseline. It runs the current code with current kernels: the
  unfused scorer is today's bound-aware per-head FP32 fallback (about 108 ms per 128K call,
  CUDA-event timing), the pre-#6206 device layout costs about 25–29 ms per 128K CP32 call
  (synchronized timing of the device builder, adjusted for in-run contention), and the explicit
  cuDNN causal offsets (row 17) stay on. Two millisecond-scale leftovers remain and are not
  subtracted: P0 still builds the inverse key permutation on every DSA call although nothing
  consumes it, and still copies the host `cu_seqlens` at batch time although its layout path
  ignores them.
- P0 and P1 eager times include eager-only host costs on the current code: the HybridEP
  token-count equalization sync on every dispatch, variable-shape PP send/recv and, in P0, per-rank
  layout synchronizations. P1 → P2 removes them together with the graph, so it is not a pure graph
  gain.
- The MTP optimizations are part of the baseline by choice. Repeated-MTP KV and top-k sharing is
  part of the model and stays on.
- Only the eager stages run the runner's read-only host-side observers on their timed steps (graph
  replay skips them); their bound is at most 0.014% of a step.
- Numerics are not bitwise across stages: the MXFP8/DeepGEMM scorer selects different keys, MoK
  (BF16 shared experts) and HybridEP (GLU32 expert layout) compute the MoE layers differently, and
  forced-balance routing draws its random numbers in execution order. The routing map is realized
  as `bool` in P0–P3 and natively by MoK in P4.
- Execution-adjusted TF is not computed for P0: its per-head scorer is outside the metrics tool's
  execution ledger. Eager rates (P0, P1) are wall-time rates. As in the formal cells, the upper end
  adds a bound for MoK routed-FC1 replay; the tool applies it to every stage, including P1–P3,
  which do not run MoK.
- One allocation, one window per cell and a fixed order (no ABBA); P4a and P4b bracket the job.

### What the profiles show

**Current time budget** (profiled iteration 8, stage medians of the sampled ranks).

| Trained cell | Profiled step, NVTX median (s) | Layer compute + MoK, share | Fill/drain bubble (s) | Stage imbalance (s) | Outside graph, unprofiled estimate (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K | 13.764 | 80% | 1.056 | 0.377 | 1.015 |
| 128K | 15.892 | 79% | 1.256 | 0.615 | 0.686 |
| 1M | 25.122 | 74% | 3.836 | 0.533 | 0.610 |

- **Pipeline.** PP1 is the critical stage in every cell; PP2 ties it at 4K and 128K. PP3 (MTP7,
  output head and loss) is not critical. With stages starting only on top-k-computing layers, an
  exhaustive schedule simulation (within −20 to +78 ms of the measured graph spans) finds the
  current layouts optimal.
- **Outside the graph.** The pre-graph phase is CPU-bound. At 4K its critical path is the
  dynamic-CP reroute on PP3, which copies all 2,048 local samples per key and keeps about 2%. All
  ranks wait for it in the full-iteration graph's WORLD capture-signature check
  (`FullCudaGraphWrapper._check_capture_signature`), not in the packing scheduler, whose DP
  all-gathers launch no kernel at DP size 1. The post-graph phase (~0.6 s) is paced by the Muon
  step's CPU launch rate on the rank with the most small matrices: a per-head Newton–Schulz loop
  over the MLA up-projections, 128 calls per matrix.
- **Communication.** NCCL never overlaps other GPU work. PP send/recv time is waiting, not
  transfer. The in-layer CP all-gather and reduce-scatter are fully exposed.
- **Kernels.** Utilization figures are modelled from kernel times and FLOPs or bytes, not measured
  with hardware counters.
  - On the bottleneck stage MoK is the largest family (27–36% of the graph), the sparse-attention
    backward the largest compute family (21–24%).
  - The sparse-attention backward reaches about 25% of BF16 peak at 4K/128K and 16–19% at 1M, the
    forward 42–44%; the backward takes 4.3–5.3x the forward time for 2.53x the FLOPs.
  - At 1M the backward per call rises from 21.8 ms at CP position 0 to 28.0 ms at position 63
    (modelled as key-range L2 locality), and faster ranks wait about 0.5–0.7 s per stage per
    step.
  - The DeepGEMM scorer reaches 46 / 62 / 60% of FP8 peak (4K / 128K / 1M); MXFP8 projections
    63–71%. Layout copies take 5.8–7.4% of the bottleneck graph.
  - With the MXFP8 indexer, the trained indexer loss runs two score-recompute kernels per indexer
    call: the 64-head recompute and a 32-head FP32 recompute that the MXFP8 loss requires.

**Frozen vs trained.** Same code and layout; the formal saving (0.912 / 1.224 / 1.443 s) is
indexer-loss work: score recompute 0.27 / 0.45 / 0.58 s, indexer backward 0.18 / 0.20 / 0.29 s,
the extra LSE-only sparse forward 0.15 / 0.22 / 0.29 s, loss elementwise kernels 0.15 / 0.16 /
0.18 s. The frozen indexer's remaining cost is 0.7% / 1.7% / 5.4% of the graph.

**Remaining opportunities** (model estimates per step, not measured; nothing is implemented, and
optimization work is paused), low effort and strong evidence first:
1. Copy only the received samples in the dynamic-CP reroute, then prepare step n+1's data during
   the graph replay: about 0.4 s at 4K, at most 0.13 s elsewhere.
2. Batch the per-head Newton–Schulz of the MLA up-projections in Muon: about 0.15 s.
3. Trained indexer: drop the extra LSE-only sparse forward: 0.16–0.28 s.
4. Drop the redundant top-k compaction sort: 0.05–0.08 s.
5. Remove avoidable layout copies around absorbed MLA and the CP all-gather: 0.31–0.45 s.
6. Larger: the sparse-attention backward kernel (0.3–1.0 s), 1-layer stage boundaries with a
   cross-PP top-k handoff (0.1–0.5 s), selective recompute at 1M (about 0.5 s, memory risk), and
   intra-layer overlap of the CP collectives (0.15–0.35 s).

**Not recommended.** VPP2 at 4K/128K and VPP4 (or VPP3 with MTP7 in one chunk) at 1M: the
simulation predicts slower steps in every cell except 128K trained, where it predicts a 0.04 s
saving, within model error. One score-recompute kernel: the MXFP8 indexer loss needs the second.
MXFP8 output and MTP heads: PP3 is not critical. Tuning the absorbed-MLA BF16 batched
GEMMs: they are memory-bound (modelled at 75–85% of the HBM roofline).

**Limits.** Only 4 of 64 ranks per stage were profiled, so stage maxima may lie on unsampled
ranks. The formal graph replay is assumed equal to the profiled span. Two collectives are
identified only by order and size. Open measurements: a formal 4K VPP2 run, ncu and per-rank
timing of the 1M sparse-attention backward across CP positions, and CUDA-event timers in an
unprofiled run.

## GPU-run opt-in flags

Recipe `ARGS` keys are listed; on the command line they are `--hyphen-case`. Everything is off by
default except the score-fill skip.

| Option | Default | Native recipes | Measured 256-GPU cells | Requirements and notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pipeline_model_parallel_prewarm` | off | on | on | #6850 + rows 7/8; PP > 1 |
| `cuda_graph_impl: full_iteration`, `cuda_graph_static_dynamic_cp` | `none` / off | on | on | #5807 + rows 35/36: THD packing with `pad_packed_seq_alignment: max`; HybridEP needs no `moe_hybridep_pad_variable_tokens` here. With VPP, validated only with batched PP send/recv (`no_overlap_p2p_communication`). |
| `no_overlap_p2p_communication` | off | 1M | 1M VPP2 cells | Upstream flag; the 1M interleaved recipe sets it (see above) |
| `mtp_repeated_layer_shared_components: [latent_kv, sparse_attention_index]` | unset | on | on | #6472/#7107 + row 37; GPT MTP path only |
| `dsa_indexer_precision: mxfp8` | `bf16` | on | on | Row 29 packed-THD MXFP8 scorer: TE MXFP8 and indexer head dim 128. The indexer-loss scores are recomputed in FP32 from the BF16 inputs. |
| `dsa_indexer_scorer_backend: deepgemm` | `cudnn` | on | on | Row 33. Needs `mxfp8`, `deep_gemm >= 2.8.1` (perf stack 2.8.2+5081f85), SM 10.3, cuDNN FE >= 1.29, and 32/64 indexer heads of dim 128. Otherwise it falls back to the cuDNN MXFP8 scorer with the warning `dsa_indexer_scorer_backend='deepgemm' is unavailable`; the confirmation "DSA indexer scorer uses DeepGEMM" logs at INFO level. With an active or frozen indexer loss, full or `core_attn` recompute requires `dsa_indexer_reuse_checkpoint_topk`. |
| `dsa_indexer_topk_backend: deepselect` | `cudnn` | on | on | Rows 31/32: needs an external DeepSelect build (perf stack: DeepSelect `bfa4507` with local tuning patches). Never used in deterministic mode; narrow rows keep cuDNN. |
| `dsa_indexer_reuse_checkpoint_topk` | off | 1M | on at 1M and in the 1-node smokes | Row 26: the recompute replay reuses the first call's top-k (with a frozen indexer, it also skips the indexer). |
| `dsa_indexer_loss_coeff: "0"` | recipe `1e-2` | `1e-2`; `0` with `--variant frozen_indexer` | frozen cells | Frozen-indexer cells |
| `dsa_indexer_skip_masked_score_fill` | on | default | default (patch installed; no cuDNN scorer call ran) | Row 28. Takes effect only when the cuDNN FE `indexer_forward_wrapper` has `clean_logits` (NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1761, draft) and FE >= 1.29; otherwise the prefill is kept. `--no-dsa-indexer-skip-masked-score-fill` restores the prefill. |
| `dataloader_prefetch_factor` | dev #5771 window | default | default | Row 16; `2` restores PyTorch's default window |
| `deterministic_mode` | off | off | off | Rows 18/30: deterministic cuDNN DSA; the `tie_break` top-k needs cuDNN FE >= 1.31 (older versions keep the full-row canonicalization). Related: #7813. |

## Metric scope and qualification limits

- **Logged/model TFLOPS:** logical model arithmetic on valid tokens/lengths,
  including detached MTP heads; FMA=2. No precision weighting or recompute charge.
- **Execution-adjusted TFLOPS:** valid-pair defining GEMMs and accounted replay/
  recompute, plus the declared norm proxies. Excludes padding/tile inflation,
  router GEMMs, other elementwise/communication/optimizer work; not instruction
  counting or peak utilization. Unlogged MoK replay gives an interval, not
  an exact point. Use step time/tokens for speedup, not inflated replay TFLOPS.
- **Nonfinite-performance policy:** NaN/Inf loss or gradient-norm observations may be kept as
  numerical metadata, never as correctness or convergence evidence, and never waive timing,
  step/microbatch, sparse-capacity, topology, backend or capture/replay checks. A shortened top-k
  workload, dropped routes, fallback, CUDA/NCCL error or other structural failure invalidates the
  cell. Nothing is sanitized to obtain a result.
- Allocator maxima include warmup/capture. Device-used is sampled on all 256
  ranks after steps 1/2/32, not continuously; retain per-rank/PP-stage evidence.
- Full-iteration graphs apply to fixed realized packing, effective shape and
  microbatch counts. Enabled dynamic CP does not establish arbitrary changing
  CP/shape/microbatch graph support.
- The formal jobs control the allocation within each length, but each runs its cells once, in a
  fixed order; this is not ABBA evidence. No drift qualification is claimed. Every allocation is
  labeled and no cross-allocation ratio is claimed as a controlled causal speedup.
- Resolved commands, source/image/dependency identities, native YAML checksums,
  topology and raw logs remain in the experiment evidence.

> [!CAUTION]
> Tracking-only integration PR. **DO NOT MERGE.**
> Pending capabilities must be reviewed and merged through their source PRs.

# GLM-5.2 integration tracking and GB300 full-model performance

Updated 2026-11-01.

**Head: `edebb6b2d9e8425f164ee0365260ed99b12e0829`, 39 stack commits on
`dev@a5aa637fa5dbe2b08af7b413e32306dbc086aa01`.** The tracking branch and the development branch
are both at this head. It replaces `42779557cc` with a new revision of the recipe commit (row 39),
whose recipes now carry the formal cells' DSA flags, runtime stack and Slurm launch; rows 1–38 are
unchanged. The base includes the main-to-dev sync
[#7960](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7960). Dev has also merged the nightly sync
[#8402](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8402); the stack is not yet rebased onto it.
Among other conflict resolutions, that rebase drops the MTP-tracker hunk of row 35 (main #7768
arrives with #8402) and needs a `get_run_config` stub in row 14's test.

Status at the head (details below):
- **CPU.** Per-commit gates over all 39 commits, run at `2d7d052aee`. That commit has the head's
  code and tests; the head differs from it only in the recipes under `examples/`.
- **GPU.** A 1-node GB300 smoke at `42779557cc`, which has the head's code, passes. The GPU unit
  items, a 4-node proxy pre-gate and the 1M VPP2 parity proof ran at `2c9bd94108`, whose model code
  differs from the head only in the config-time layout check and an FE version gate that is inert
  on the measured FE 1.31.
- **Performance.** The six formal 256-GPU cells of the current recipes were measured at
  `2c9bd94108` (4K, 1M) and `2d7d052aee` (128K), through an internal runner. **Run as their README
  says, without the runner, the head's recipes reproduce all six cells: medians within 0.11%** (job
  `50951`, unprofiled; see "The recipe run"). A 128K stage ablation at `42779557cc` (job `12654`,
  unprofiled, not a formal run) reproduces the 128K trained cell within 0.06% (see "128K stage
  ablation at the previous head").
- **NSys at the head's code.** Two 64-node profiling jobs at `42779557cc` cover all six cells (96
  reports). Their last unprofiled steps are within 0.21% of the formal medians: consistency
  evidence, not a formal measurement.

Profiles are not timing qualification; the unprofiled tables (the formal cells, the recipe run and
the 128K stage ablation) are the only performance claims in this PR. Publishing the development
refs does not mark this tracking-only PR ready for merge.

Tracking branch: `buptzyb:codex/tracking/glm5-2-integration`.
Long-lived development branch: `buptzyb:codex/glm5-2-dev`.
Component links below preserve source provenance.

## Integration stack

Base: `dev@a5aa637fa5dbe2b08af7b413e32306dbc086aa01`.
Head: `edebb6b2d9e8425f164ee0365260ed99b12e0829`.
Tree: `164f7237187756c170cc7b192bf1cb6d24c58952`.
There are 39 commits above the base:
- five source-PR snapshots;
- six glue commits;
- 18 upstream candidates;
- nine local commits;
- one recipe commit.

They are not 39 independent PRs. Every commit is GPG-signed with a DCO sign-off.
Row numbers are stack positions, counted from the base.

The commits are ordered in eight layers: source-PR snapshots, glue, general fixes, DSA base, DSA
dataflow, scoring and top-k, full-iteration CUDA Graph, and recipes. The full-iteration CUDA Graph
layer (#5807 and its fixes) sits above all other code, so no lower commit depends on it.

- **Candidate, standalone** means the commit applies to dev `a5aa637fa5` on its own.
- **Candidate, on ...** lists what the commit needs on dev. With those commits, it applies

- **Local** commits stay in this stack for now.

No upstream PR has been opened for the candidates yet.

### Notes on individual commits

- **Row 15.** Main #6754 (in the base through #7960) runs the synchronous LayerWise MXFP8
  parameter sync through the DDP bucket groups with `grad_data` as the receive buffer. Row 15
  keeps only the per-parameter staging into the receive slot and the equal-size tensor all-gather.
- **Rows 17 and 18.** Row 17 adapts the cuDNN DSA call sites to the FE >= 1.26 defaults: global
  sparse top-k ids (`topk_indices_global=True`) and explicit bottom-right causal offsets, passed
  from FE 1.26, the release that changed the default. CPU fakes cover both frontend generations.
  Row 18 makes cuDNN DSA deterministic on top of row 17 and carries the `+inf` top-k membership
  fix.
- **Row 22.** A layer that runs KPool selection
  ([#8287](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8287)) without tail selection does not
  certify its top-k rows as non-empty. Its CPU test needs only dev.
- **Row 23.** `TransformerConfig` checks a custom `pipeline_model_parallel_layout` at parse time,
  on every rank. With `dsa_indexer_topk_freq > 1`, it rejects a layout whose pipeline stage or
  virtual stage starts on a DSA index-sharing layer. Such a layout therefore fails at parse time,
  on CPU and on every rank, rather than at model build or the first forward, on the GPU and only
  on the ranks that own the bad chunk.
- **Row 35** also fixes the test double
  `TestThdStaticPPCommunicationShapes::test_get_tensor_shapes_uses_static_thd_width`. Its config
  lacked `pipeline_model_parallel_size`, which dev reads (main #7336, synced through #7960).
- **Row 38** covers interleaved (VPP) THD full-iteration plumbing on CPU: the schedule shape and
  layout, dynamic-CP scheduling per model chunk, the per-(chunk, microbatch) static slots, and the
  dynamic-CP certificate across VPP slots.
- **Row 39** holds the native recipes (layouts under "Native full-model recipes") and their Slurm
  and Pyxis launch. It replaces `42779557cc`, whose recipes lacked the formal cells' DSA flags,
  runtime stack and launch (see "The recipe run").

### Behaviour adapted to current dev

Each snapshot is one squash-pick of its upstream PR, adapted to the current dev, so its tree does
not equal the PR head; the upstream PRs are based on older dev. The #6741 snapshot keeps its
sequence-roll code in `mtp_sequence_roll.py`. Adaptations that change behaviour (each is recorded
in its commit message):
- #6472: dev runs TransformerBlock full recompute through the common `megatron.core.recompute`
  (main #6648). The forward-sharing checkpoint wrapper lives there, so it also wraps HybridStack
  full recompute when forward sharing is enabled.
- #6741: absolute MTP rows are used only when there is no `mtp_input_mask`, no precomputed MTP
  `decoder_input`, and the attention CP layout is not `contiguous`. In all other cases dev's
  cumulative roll runs.
- THD full-iteration graphs and main #7046's HybridEP check: the check requires
  `moe_hybridep_pad_variable_tokens` for sequence packing and exempts
  `cuda_graph_impl='full_iteration'`, whose static inputs already pad every rank to
  `max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank`.
- RNG generators are registered at capture only when dev's
  `cudagraph_needs_generator_registration()` asks for it (main #7348).
- Static-certified dynamic CP (row 36) follows dev's CP1 contract from main #7045:
  `cp_group=None` plus `cp_singleton_group`.
- The DeepGEMM scorer (row 33) needs `deep_gemm >= 2.8.1`. Dev's `batch_invariant` extra pins
  2.8.0, which falls back to the cuDNN MXFP8 scorer.

### Dependencies

- **Base.** `dev@a5aa637fa5` ([#8232](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8232)) includes
  the main-to-dev sync #7960 and [#8287](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8287) (KPool
  DSA indexer, NoPE MLA and FP8 indexer precision controls; dev port of main #7522). The stack inherits
  [fixed-shape DSA sparse backward](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7434),
  [detached MTP-head FLOPs correction](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7604),
  [TV/fusion](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6473) and
  [per-head Muon](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7085) from dev and does not duplicate
  them.
- **Pending dev sync.** [#8402](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8402) is merged into
  dev; the stack is not yet rebased onto it (see the top of this description).
- **Open source PRs carried as snapshots.** #6472 at `f5ada3564`, #7107 at `741fc442e`, #6741 at
  `a833ab16e`, #6850 at `b3a749511` and #5807 at `26d0e6794` (rows 1–4 and 34).
- **Open PRs that overlap.**

## Native full-model recipes

256 GB300, 78 decoder layers (3 dense + 75 MoE), 256 experts,
TP1/PP4/EP64/configured CP64 (1M: interleaved, two virtual stages per PP rank),
packed THD/dynamic CP, shared repeated MTP7
E2E-TV with detached heads, per-head Muon, force balance and MoK. No offload.
MXFP8 covers eligible projection/grouped GEMMs, MoK routed experts and the DSA
indexer's key scoring (DeepGEMM). MoK shared experts use BF16, with FP8 execution
and FP8 parameter storage disabled; cuDNN DSA sparse attention remains BF16, with
FP32 reductions/state where required. This is a performance
recipe, not long-term convergence or complete official optimizer-parity evidence.
Data uses NullTokenizer and fixed-length varlen mock samples with force-balanced
routing; these results do not establish real-data performance or convergence.

| Property | 4K | 128K | 1M |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Nominal sequence limit | 4,096 | 131,072 | 1,048,576 |
| Valid post-shift tokens/sample | 3,968 | 126,976 | 1,015,808 |
| Effective CP / DP | 1 / 64 | 32 / 2 | 64 / 1 |
| GBS / MBS | 2,048 / 1 | 64 / 1 | 8 / 1 |
| Realized microbatches/step | 32 | 32 | 8 |
| Local valid tokens / capacity | 3,968 / 4,096 | 3,968 / 4,096 | 15,872 / 16,384 |
| Valid global tokens/step | 8,126,464 | 8,126,464 | 8,126,464 |
| Decoder layers per PP rank + MTP7 | 22/24/24/8 + 7 | 22/24/24/8 + 7 | 22/24/20/12 + 7 (VPP2) |
| Pipeline schedule | 1F1B | 1F1B | Interleaved, batched PP send/recv |
| Recompute | Layernorm only | Layernorm only | Full uniform1 |
| MoK mini / macro | 4,096 / 40,960 | 4,096 / 40,960 | 4,096 / 131,072 |

Pipeline layouts:
- 4K and 128K: `Et*22|t*24|t*24|t*8m*7L` (1F1B). PP3 also holds MTP7 and the output head, so it
  carries the fewest decoder layers.
- 1M: `Et*10|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*8|m*7L`, interleaved with two virtual stages per PP rank
  (22/24/20/12 decoder layers per rank). It sets `no_overlap_p2p_communication`, because
  full-iteration CUDA Graphs are validated with batched PP send/recv only.
- With index sharing every fourth layer, every stage and virtual stage must start at a layer that
  computes its own top-k, so stage boundaries can only move in steps of four layers (the current
  chunks start at decoder layers 1, 23, 47 and 71, and at 1M at 1, 11, 23, 35, 47, 59 and 71).
  Row 23 enforces this at config time.

Recipes: `examples/moe_recipes/glm5_2/gb300/`
`mxfp8_THD{4K,128K,1M}_256GPU_TP1PP4EP64CP64_full_cg_mok.yaml`;
renderer: `examples/moe_recipes/glm5_2/run.py`; Slurm launch: `srun_rank.sh` and
`check_placement.py` next to it. Their README gives the runtime artifacts, the launch steps and
the validation scope (the formal cells and the recipe run).
Actual topology places each EP64 group within one of four NVL domains.
The sweep compares runnable recipes. Local tokens, CP, microbatch count, PP split, schedule and
recompute differ across lengths, not just sequence length.

## Formal 256-GPU results

Every job in this section ran on one GB300 NVL72 cluster.

- **Protocol.**
  - No profiler. 32 optimizer steps: steps 1–3 are eager warmup and step 4 is the graph capture.
  - All 20 samples from steps 13–32 are kept, with no outlier or GC deletion.
  - p95 is nearest-rank and CV is the population CV. Every cell in this section passes CV <= 2%
    and the in-job validator.
  - Memory is in GiB for the worst PP stage, given as allocated / reserved high-water / sampled
    maximum device-used. Device-used is sampled after steps 1, 2 and 32 on all 256 ranks.
    nvidia-smi reports 277.55 GiB per GB300.
- **Stack.** The runtime libraries listed under "Dependencies", the same in every job. The
  `clean_logits` patch was not exercised: DeepGEMM scored every indexer call, so no cuDNN scorer
  call ran.
- **Configuration.**
  - The native recipes of their source commits, plus three opt-in flags in every cell:
    `dsa_indexer_precision: mxfp8`, `dsa_indexer_scorer_backend: deepgemm` and
    `dsa_indexer_topk_backend: deepselect`. The 1M cells also set
    `dsa_indexer_reuse_checkpoint_topk`. The head's recipes set these flags themselves.
  - Each length runs with the indexer trained (`dsa_indexer_loss_coeff` `1e-2`, the recipe value)
    and frozen (`"0"`).
  - DeepSelect runs at 128K and 1M. At 4K every row is narrower than the BF16 tuning table, so
    top-k stays on cuDNN, as designed.
- **Placement.** Each 64-node job puts every PP stage on 16 nodes of one NVL72 rack.

- **Spread.** In five cells the p95 and CV come mostly from steps 21 and 31, after the manual GC,
  as in the formal cells. In 1M frozen, steps 27 and 29 took 0.44 and 0.36 s longer than the
  median, for no reason that the log shows; they set its p95 and raise its CV from 0.50% to
  0.67%, but move its median by 4 ms.
- **Environment.** Ranks 0 and 255 recorded the environment they start with in the training steps'
  layout and container. Their `OMP_*` and `NCCL_*` variables were the cluster's enroot settings
  (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` and the site's NCCL network and logging settings), `NCCL_VERSION` from the
  image and `NCCL_INSPECTOR_DUMP_DIR`, whose source is unknown; that variable does nothing without
  `NCCL_INSPECTOR_ENABLE`, which neither the recorded environment nor the recipes set. The formal
  jobs did not record their ranks' environment.

## 128K stage ablation at the previous head

In this section, the head is `42779557cc`, the previous head, which has the current head's code;
the job set each stage's arguments at run time, with the formal cells' DSA flags from P3 on.

One 64-node job (256 GB300) at the head (`12654`, completed `0:0`, 7,202 s) measured how much each
part of the current 128K trained recipe contributes, starting from a true-eager baseline. It uses
the timing protocol of the formal cells (32 steps, all 20 samples of steps 13–32, CV <= 2%), the
indexer trained and the layout `Et*22|t*24|t*24|t*8m*7L` in every stage. Each stage adds one group
of features to the stage before it; each cell is its own launch, in the order P4a, P3, P2, P1, P0,
P4b. Every cell passed the in-job and local validators (graph mode and capture count, DSA layout
path, scorer and top-k paths, the behaviour of rows 12, 24 and 27, MTP absolute-row addressing,
HybridEP topology, no paged-stash overflow) and the CV gate.

| Stage | Adds | Code | Graph | Median / p95 (s) | CV | Model TF/GPU | Execution-adjusted TF/GPU | Tokens/s/GPU | PP0 max allocated / sampled device-used (GiB) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P0 | Baseline: HybridEP with paged stash, MTP optimizations on, per-call DSA layout and unfused per-head scorer, other DSA optimizations off | head + 3 patches | eager | 71.910 / 72.617 | 0.355% | 166.8 | not computed | 441.4 | 232.5 / 253.7 |
| P1 | + #6206 host layout, per-microbatch memo and packed fused scorer | head + 2 patches | eager | 27.553 / 28.296 | 1.055% | 435.3 | 461.4–499.4 | 1,152.1 | 232.4 / 254.2 |
| P2 | + prebuilt packed-CP layout tables and full-iteration CUDA Graph | head + 1 patch | captured | 19.428 / 19.844 | 0.675% | 617.4 | 654.3–708.3 | 1,633.9 | 232.5 / 257.3 |
| P3 | + other DSA optimizations | head | captured | 16.735 / 17.150 | 0.790% | 716.7 | 760.3–822.9 | 1,896.8 | 232.5 / 256.1 |
| P4a | + MoK: the current recipe | head | captured | 15.728 / 16.136 | 0.831% | 762.6 | 809.0–875.6 | 2,018.4 | 226.9 / 244.8 |
| P4b | P4 again, last in the job | head | captured | 15.720 / 16.139 | 0.817% | 763.0 | 809.4–876.1 | 2,019.4 | 226.9 / 244.7 |

Model TF/GPU is the logged model numerator, the same in every stage, over the step time.

**Transitions.** Fixed before the run: a direction is claimed only if the longest step of the faster
cell is shorter than the shortest step of the slower cell; a P4a/P4b drift above 1% would leave
smaller deltas unresolved; a diagnostic second comparison drops the two manual-GC steps (21 and
31); P0 and P1 may each be repeated once, only for a repeatable failure of their window.
- P0 → P1, #6206 host layout, memo and packed fused scorer (eager): −44.358 s (−61.68%), faster.
- P1 → P2, prebuilt layout tables and the full-iteration CUDA Graph: −8.125 s (−29.49%), faster.
- P2 → P3, other DSA optimizations: −2.693 s (−13.86%), faster.
- P3 → P4, MoK: −1.007 s (−6.02%; P4b −1.015 s), faster.
- Every transition separates by the rule, and the comparison without the GC steps agrees. The
  P4a/P4b drift is 0.05% and both eager windows qualified, so no repeat ran. Overall, P0 → P4 goes
  from 71.91 to 15.73 s per step: 4.57x tokens/s (441 → 2,018). Of the 56.18 s reduction, the four
  transitions take 79%, 14%, 5% and 2%.

**What each stage changes.**
- P0–P2 ran the head plus local, experiment-only feature-disabling patches (not part of this
  stack); P3 and P4 ran the head unchanged.
  - In P0–P2, one patch reverts #6166's invalid-slot handling and turns off the inverse-permutation
    backward (row 24) and top-k certificate sharing (row 27).
  - In P0, one patch turns off the packed fused indexer scorer, so every call takes the bound-aware
    unfused per-head fallback (FP32 matmuls; BF16 indexer only). This per-head path is the
    intended P0 stage definition and the validators require it on every call; it is not an
    unintended fallback in the sense of "Metric scope and qualification limits" below.
  - In P0, one patch restores the pre-#6206 DSA layout: the packed-CP layout is built on the
    device, per rank, on every DSA call, with no host layout, memo or prebuilt tables.
  - In P1, one patch turns off only the prebuilt layout tables; the #6206 host layout is built once
    per microbatch and memoized.
  - The layout patches change timing only: in CPU tests the layout tables and the DSA forward
    inputs are bitwise identical to the head's.
- P0 and P1 are true eager (no full-iteration graph, no static dynamic CP), with HybridEP padding
  variable token counts, as eager HybridEP requires. P2–P4 run the native full-iteration graph,
  captured at step 4.
- P0–P3 use HybridEP with paged stash (rank capacity factor 1.2, GLU32 expert layout) instead of
  MoK; P4 is the native recipe.
- P1 and P2 score with the BF16 cuDNN packed fused scorer, including its `-inf` prefill. P3 adds
  #6166, rows 24 and 27, the MXFP8 indexer with the DeepGEMM scorer, and DeepSelect top-k; the
  prefill goes away with DeepGEMM, which never pre-fills (the row 28 skip is inert in every
  stage).
- The MTP optimizations, #6741 absolute-row addressing and the shard-only shared-embedding gradient
  all-reduce (row 12), are on in every stage.
- P4 runs the launch arguments of the 128K trained formal cell on the same 64 nodes as job `12015`
  and reproduces it: 15.728 / 15.720 s against 15.72805 s, 226.9 GiB max allocated in both.

**How to read it.**
- Stage gains depend on the order of the stages: each delta is measured on top of the stages before
  it.
- P0 is not a pure historical baseline. It runs the current code with current kernels: the
  unfused scorer is today's bound-aware per-head FP32 fallback (about 108 ms per 128K call,
  CUDA-event timing), the pre-#6206 device layout costs about 25–29 ms per 128K CP32 call
  (synchronized timing of the device builder, adjusted for in-run contention), and the explicit
  cuDNN causal offsets (row 17) stay on. Two millisecond-scale leftovers remain and are not
  subtracted: P0 still builds the inverse key permutation on every DSA call although nothing
  consumes it, and still copies the host `cu_seqlens` at batch time although its layout path
  ignores them.
- P0 and P1 eager times include eager-only host costs on the current code: the HybridEP
  token-count equalization sync on every dispatch, variable-shape PP send/recv and, in P0, per-rank
  layout synchronizations. P1 → P2 removes them together with the graph, so it is not a pure graph
  gain.
- The MTP optimizations are part of the baseline by choice. Repeated-MTP KV and top-k sharing is
  part of the model and stays on.
- Only the eager stages run the runner's read-only host-side observers on their timed steps (graph
  replay skips them); their bound is at most 0.014% of a step.
- Numerics are not bitwise across stages: the MXFP8/DeepGEMM scorer selects different keys, MoK
  (BF16 shared experts) and HybridEP (GLU32 expert layout) compute the MoE layers differently, and
  forced-balance routing draws its random numbers in execution order. The routing map is realized
  as `bool` in P0–P3 and natively by MoK in P4.
- Execution-adjusted TF is not computed for P0: its per-head scorer is outside the metrics tool's
  execution ledger. Eager rates (P0, P1) are wall-time rates. As in the formal cells, the upper end
  adds a bound for MoK routed-FC1 replay; the tool applies it to every stage, including P1–P3,
  which do not run MoK.
- One allocation, one window per cell and a fixed order (no ABBA); P4a and P4b bracket the job.

## NSys profiles at the previous head

The profiles at `42779557cc` (the previous head, which has the current head's code) are separate
from the formal rows above, are not timing-qualified, and do not replace them. The unprofiled
tables remain the only timing measurements in this PR; profiled steps and model estimates below
are diagnostic.

- **Jobs.** Probe `12037` (1 node, reduced smoke model, trained, 2 reports, 300 s); `12039`
  (64 nodes, 1,926 s; 4K and 128K) and `12041` (64 nodes, 1,768 s; 1M), indexer trained and
  frozen; all `0:0` on the cluster of the formal jobs.
- **Protocol.** The formal launch arguments of each cell plus only the profiler arguments: 11 steps, graph
  capture at step 4, `--profile-step-start 6 --profile-step-end 8` (iterations 7 and 8 captured).
  Nsight Systems 2026.4.1 with `--trace=cuda,nvtx`, `--capture-range=cudaProfilerApi` and
  `--cuda-graph-trace=node`; no CPU sampling, `emit_nvtx` or `record_shapes`, and two NVTX ranges
  per step. Four EP ranks per PP stage (`0,21,42,63,64,...,255`): 16 reports per cell, 96 in all.
- **Validity.** Every report has two graph launches, identical replays and no lost-, dropped- or
  overflow-event diagnostic (Nsight's generic "not all events might have been collected" warnings
  remain). In-job and local validation passed for every cell. An offline extractor checked every
  report and the probe with no failure, and caught 6 of 6 injected faults.

**Consistency with the formal rows.** Iteration 6 is the last step before the capture opens.

| Cell | Formal median, s (job) | Iteration 6, unprofiled (s) | Iteration 8, profiled (s) | Graph span, iteration 8 (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K trained | 13.50495 (`11713`) | 13.509 (+0.03%) | 13.790 (+2.11%) | 12.490 |
| 4K frozen | 12.59260 (`11713`) | 12.616 (+0.19%) | 12.853 (+2.06%) | 11.574 |
| 128K trained | 15.72805 (`12015`) | 15.762 (+0.21%) | 15.893 (+1.05%) | 15.042 |
| 128K frozen | 14.50430 (`12015`) | 14.526 (+0.15%) | 14.666 (+1.11%) | 13.798 |
| 1M trained | 25.02340 (`11749`) | 25.046 (+0.09%) | 25.122 (+0.39%) | 24.413 |
| 1M frozen | 23.58025 (`11749`) | 23.587 (+0.03%) | 23.662 (+0.34%) | 22.969 |

- Single steps without a CV gate: evidence that the head's code reproduces the formal cells
  measured at `2c9bd94108`/`2d7d052aee`, not a re-measurement. Iteration 5 is within
  −0.3% to +1.1%, except one 4K frozen step (+4.2%). Only the 128K cells ran on the nodes of their
  formal job.
- Per-stage max allocated after step 2 equals the formal jobs' value at the same point (24 of 24
  stage values); the formal end-of-run maxima are at most 64 MiB higher.
- Profiling adds up to 0.28 s per step, in CPU-bound eager phases. Between iterations 7 and 8,
  graph spans differ by +0.15% to +0.53% and per-call kernel times agree (only the MoK barrier
  wait drifts); iteration 7 absorbs the profiler-start skew, so iteration 8 is the reference.

### What the profiles show

**Current time budget** (profiled iteration 8, stage medians of the sampled ranks).

| Trained cell | Profiled step, NVTX median (s) | Layer compute + MoK, share | Fill/drain bubble (s) | Stage imbalance (s) | Outside graph, unprofiled estimate (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K | 13.764 | 80% | 1.056 | 0.377 | 1.015 |
| 128K | 15.892 | 79% | 1.256 | 0.615 | 0.686 |
| 1M | 25.122 | 74% | 3.836 | 0.533 | 0.610 |

- **Pipeline.** PP1 is the critical stage in every cell; PP2 ties it at 4K and 128K. PP3 (MTP7,
  output head and loss) is not critical. With stages starting only on top-k-computing layers, an
  exhaustive schedule simulation (within −20 to +78 ms of the measured graph spans) finds the
  current layouts optimal.
- **Outside the graph.** The pre-graph phase is CPU-bound. At 4K its critical path is the
  dynamic-CP reroute on PP3, which copies all 2,048 local samples per key and keeps about 2%. All
  ranks wait for it in the full-iteration graph's WORLD capture-signature check
  (`FullCudaGraphWrapper._check_capture_signature`), not in the packing scheduler, whose DP
  all-gathers launch no kernel at DP size 1. The post-graph phase (~0.6 s) is paced by the Muon
  step's CPU launch rate on the rank with the most small matrices: a per-head Newton–Schulz loop
  over the MLA up-projections, 128 calls per matrix.
- **Communication.** NCCL never overlaps other GPU work. PP send/recv time is waiting, not
  transfer. The in-layer CP all-gather and reduce-scatter are fully exposed.
- **Kernels.** Utilization figures are modelled from kernel times and FLOPs or bytes, not measured
  with hardware counters.
  - On the bottleneck stage MoK is the largest family (27–36% of the graph), the sparse-attention
    backward the largest compute family (21–24%).
  - The sparse-attention backward reaches about 25% of BF16 peak at 4K/128K and 16–19% at 1M, the
    forward 42–44%; the backward takes 4.3–5.3x the forward time for 2.53x the FLOPs.
  - At 1M the backward per call rises from 21.8 ms at CP position 0 to 28.0 ms at position 63
    (modelled as key-range L2 locality), and faster ranks wait about 0.5–0.7 s per stage per
    step.
  - The DeepGEMM scorer reaches 46 / 62 / 60% of FP8 peak (4K / 128K / 1M); MXFP8 projections
    63–71%. Layout copies take 5.8–7.4% of the bottleneck graph.
  - With the MXFP8 indexer, the trained indexer loss runs two score-recompute kernels per indexer
    call: the 64-head recompute and a 32-head FP32 recompute that the MXFP8 loss requires.

**Frozen vs trained.** Same code and layout; the formal saving (0.912 / 1.224 / 1.443 s) is
indexer-loss work: score recompute 0.27 / 0.45 / 0.58 s, indexer backward 0.18 / 0.20 / 0.29 s,
the extra LSE-only sparse forward 0.15 / 0.22 / 0.29 s, loss elementwise kernels 0.15 / 0.16 /
0.18 s. The frozen indexer's remaining cost is 0.7% / 1.7% / 5.4% of the graph.

**Remaining opportunities** (model estimates per step, not measured; nothing is implemented, and
optimization work is paused), low effort and strong evidence first:
1. Copy only the received samples in the dynamic-CP reroute, then prepare step n+1's data during
   the graph replay: about 0.4 s at 4K, at most 0.13 s elsewhere.
2. Batch the per-head Newton–Schulz of the MLA up-projections in Muon: about 0.15 s.
3. Trained indexer: drop the extra LSE-only sparse forward: 0.16–0.28 s.
4. Drop the redundant top-k compaction sort: 0.05–0.08 s.
5. Remove avoidable layout copies around absorbed MLA and the CP all-gather: 0.31–0.45 s.
6. Larger: the sparse-attention backward kernel (0.3–1.0 s), 1-layer stage boundaries with a
   cross-PP top-k handoff (0.1–0.5 s), selective recompute at 1M (about 0.5 s, memory risk), and
   intra-layer overlap of the CP collectives (0.15–0.35 s).

**Not recommended.** VPP2 at 4K/128K and VPP4 (or VPP3 with MTP7 in one chunk) at 1M: the
simulation predicts slower steps in every cell except 128K trained, where it predicts a 0.04 s
saving, within model error. One score-recompute kernel: the MXFP8 indexer loss needs the second.
MXFP8 output and MTP heads: PP3 is not critical. Tuning the absorbed-MLA BF16 batched
GEMMs: they are memory-bound (modelled at 75–85% of the HBM roofline).

**Limits.** Only 4 of 64 ranks per stage were profiled, so stage maxima may lie on unsampled
ranks. The formal graph replay is assumed equal to the profiled span. Two collectives are
identified only by order and size. Open measurements: a formal 4K VPP2 run, ncu and per-rank
timing of the 1M sparse-attention backward across CP positions, and CUDA-event timers in an
unprofiled run.

## GPU-run opt-in flags

Recipe `ARGS` keys are listed; on the command line they are `--hyphen-case`. Everything is off by
default except the score-fill skip.

| Option | Default | Native recipes | Measured 256-GPU cells | Requirements and notes |

| `pipeline_model_parallel_prewarm` | off | on | on | #6850 + rows 7/8; PP > 1 |
| `cuda_graph_impl: full_iteration`, `cuda_graph_static_dynamic_cp` | `none` / off | on | on | #5807 + rows 35/36: THD packing with `pad_packed_seq_alignment: max`; HybridEP needs no `moe_hybridep_pad_variable_tokens` here. With VPP, validated only with batched PP send/recv (`no_overlap_p2p_communication`). |
| `no_overlap_p2p_communication` | off | 1M | 1M VPP2 cells | Upstream flag; the 1M interleaved recipe sets it (see above) |
| `mtp_repeated_layer_shared_components: [latent_kv, sparse_attention_index]` | unset | on | on | #6472/#7107 + row 37; GPT MTP path only |
| `dsa_indexer_precision: mxfp8` | `bf16` | on | on | Row 29 packed-THD MXFP8 scorer: TE MXFP8 and indexer head dim 128. The indexer-loss scores are recomputed in FP32 from the BF16 inputs. |
| `dsa_indexer_scorer_backend: deepgemm` | `cudnn` | on | on | Row 33. Needs `mxfp8`, `deep_gemm >= 2.8.1` (perf stack 2.8.2+5081f85), SM 10.3, cuDNN FE >= 1.29, and 32/64 indexer heads of dim 128. Otherwise it falls back to the cuDNN MXFP8 scorer with the warning `dsa_indexer_scorer_backend='deepgemm' is unavailable`; the confirmation "DSA indexer scorer uses DeepGEMM" logs at INFO level. With an active or frozen indexer loss, full or `core_attn` recompute requires `dsa_indexer_reuse_checkpoint_topk`. |
| `dsa_indexer_topk_backend: deepselect` | `cudnn` | on | on | Rows 31/32: needs an external DeepSelect build (perf stack: DeepSelect `bfa4507` with local tuning patches). Never used in deterministic mode; narrow rows keep cuDNN. |
| `dsa_indexer_reuse_checkpoint_topk` | off | 1M | on at 1M and in the 1-node smokes | Row 26: the recompute replay reuses the first call's top-k (with a frozen indexer, it also skips the indexer). |

## Metric scope and qualification limits

- **Logged/model TFLOPS:** logical model arithmetic on valid tokens/lengths,
  including detached MTP heads; FMA=2. No precision weighting or recompute charge.
- **Execution-adjusted TFLOPS:** valid-pair defining GEMMs and accounted replay/
  recompute, plus the declared norm proxies. Excludes padding/tile inflation,
  router GEMMs, other elementwise/communication/optimizer work; not instruction
  counting or peak utilization. Unlogged MoK replay gives an interval, not
  an exact point. Use step time/tokens for speedup, not inflated replay TFLOPS.
- **Nonfinite-performance policy:** NaN/Inf loss or gradient-norm observations may be kept as
  numerical metadata, never as correctness or convergence evidence, and never waive timing,
  step/microbatch, sparse-capacity, topology, backend or capture/replay checks. A shortened top-k
  workload, dropped routes, fallback, CUDA/NCCL error or other structural failure invalidates the
  cell. Nothing is sanitized to obtain a result.
- Allocator maxima include warmup/capture. Device-used is sampled on all 256
  ranks after steps 1/2/32, not continuously; retain per-rank/PP-stage evidence.
- Full-iteration graphs apply to fixed realized packing, effective shape and
  microbatch counts. Enabled dynamic CP does not establish arbitrary changing
  CP/shape/microbatch graph support.
- The formal jobs control the allocation within each length, but each runs its cells once, in a
  fixed order; this is not ABBA evidence. No drift qualification is claimed. Every allocation is
  labeled and no cross-allocation ratio is claimed as a controlled causal speedup.
- Resolved commands, source/image/dependency identities, native YAML checksums,
  topology and raw logs remain in the experiment evidence.

+### THD Sequence Packing (fixed schedule)
+
+Full-iteration capture is supported with the THD sequence packing schedulers under a
+fixed-schedule, static-shape contract:
+
+- `num_microbatches` must stay constant across warmup, capture and replay. The packing scheduler
+  and dataset must produce the same number of packed microbatches every step; a change after
+  capture raises a signature-mismatch error instead of silently replaying the stale graph.
+- `--pad-packed-seq-alignment max` (or a value equal to `--max-seqlen-per-dp-cp-rank`),
+  `--max-seqlen-per-dp-cp-rank` and `--thd-max-packed-sequences` are required. Every packed
+  microbatch is canonicalized outside the graph to the per-rank token capacity and a fixed
+  `thd_max_packed_sequences + 1` cu_seqlens width; the real sequence count, `cu_seqlens` content
+  and padding distribution may still change per step when context parallel size is 1.
+- With context parallel size greater than 1, each static microbatch slot must also keep identical
+  packed boundaries across eager warmup, capture and replay. CP routes contain Python split sizes
+  and host-derived layout metadata that are baked into the graph. The batch loader validates the
+  exact boundaries and fails before capture/replay rather than reuse stale route metadata. At
+  least one eager warmup step is required so consumers can materialize host-derived device layout
+  caches before capture.
+- Dynamic context parallel remains disabled by default for full-iteration capture. A workload
+  whose realized schedule is deliberately invariant may opt in with
+  `--cuda-graph-static-dynamic-cp` together with `--dynamic-context-parallel` and
+  `--sequence-packing-scheduler default_dynamic_cp`. The flag does not make full-iteration
+  capture generally dynamic: every static microbatch slot must keep the same microbatch count,
+  effective CP size, process-group identity and ordered membership, partition mode, and (for
+  CP>1) exact packed boundaries and route-defining geometry. Layout changes are detected before
+  capture or replay and rejected by all ranks together. At effective CP1, tensor-backed
+  cu_seqlens and masks may change while the realized group remains fixed.
+- Pipeline parallel send/recv use the static CP-local token capacity instead of the per-step
+  variable-shape handshake.
+- With the interleaved schedule (VPP), every (model chunk, microbatch) pair owns its own static
+  slot, in chunk-major order (chunk `c`, microbatch `b` -> slot `c * num_microbatches + b`), and the
+  dynamic-CP certificate covers all of those slots. The packing scheduler aligns the microbatch
+  count to `microbatch_group_size_per_vp_stage`, so that aligned count must also stay constant.
+  Without `--no-overlap-p2p-communication` the interleaved schedule uses separate non-blocking
+  P2P sends and receives instead of the batched P2P path that the non-interleaved schedule
+  captures.

+## Repeated-Layer Sharing
+
+Set `mtp_use_repeated_layer: true`, `mtp_num_layers > 1`, and
+`mtp_repeated_layer_shared_components` to reuse selected results from depth 0
+at later prediction depths within the same forward and microbatch. Currently,
+this requires `experimental_attention_variant: dsa` and the repeated-layer GPT MTP path.
+
+| Shared components | Later prediction depths |
+| --- | --- |
+| omitted or `[]` | Recompute KV and follow the ordinary top-k schedule. |
+| `["latent_kv"]` | Reuse depth-0 KV; follow the ordinary top-k schedule. |
+| `["sparse_attention_index"]` | Recompute KV; reuse depth-0 top-k indices. |
+| `["latent_kv", "sparse_attention_index"]` | Reuse both depth-0 KV and top-k indices. |
+
+Queries and sparse attention are computed at every depth. Shared KV remains
+attached to autograd: consumer gradients accumulate into the depth-0 KV projection.
+This is training-time activation reuse, not inference KV caching.
+
+Ordinary IndexShare (`dsa_indexer_topk_freq` and `dsa_indexer_skip_topk_offset`)
+still determines how depth 0 obtains its indices, including reuse from an earlier
+decoder layer. Repeated-layer index sharing then reuses those indices at later
+depths. An ordinary IndexShare source must run earlier in the same PP/VPP
+execution segment; cross-PP index sharing remains unsupported. With a
+`pipeline_model_parallel_layout`, the configuration rejects a layout in which any
+PP/VPP chunk starts on a layer that reuses top-k from an earlier chunk: its first
+decoder layer, or the first MTP layer (`num_layers + 1`) of an MTP-only chunk,
+must compute its own top-k.
+
+Index sharing avoids additional indexer evaluations and auxiliary-loss contributions
+at later depths; review `dsa_indexer_loss_coeff` when changing this setting.
+It disables the combined DSA kernel, but separate fused top-k and sparse-attention
+kernels remain eligible. KV-only sharing does not itself disable the combined kernel.
+
+Compatibility:
+
+- Full uniform recompute supports sharing with `recompute_num_layers: 1`.
+  With block recompute, MTP retains its existing non-checkpointed fallback.
+- Selective recompute supports `mlp`, `moe`, `moe_act`, `shared_experts`,
+  `layernorm`, `mhc`, and `mla_up_proj`, subject to their existing requirements.
+  With KV sharing, `mla_up_proj` checkpoints Q only and retains the shared KV graph.
+- Selective `core_attn` supports index-only sharing, but not KV sharing.
+  Set `recompute_modules` explicitly for KV sharing: selective recompute defaults
+  to `core_attn`.
+- Per-layer CUDA graph scopes that capture attention are unsupported. MoE-only
+  scopes and full-iteration graphs (`cuda_graph_impl: full_iteration`) remain
+  compatible.

+## Sequence-Roll Alignment
+
+MTP reuses an immutable sequence-roll context to align input tokens, learned
+positions, padding masks, labels, and loss masks at absolute prediction offsets.
+Supported local, contiguous packed CP, and scheduler-certified one-hop zigzag or
+dynamic CP layouts share their alignment geometry. Unsupported layouts retain
+the existing cumulative-roll implementation for the complete consumer field group.
+
+Under sequence parallelism, GPT and Hybrid models preserve the unsharded padding
+mask for alignment while decoder and MTP routing consume their TP-local masks.
+The E2E-TV path reads addressed target rows directly from the source logits and
+their compact communication halo instead of materializing a full-vocabulary roll.

+# GLM-5.2 GB300 MoK recipes
+
+These native recipes package the full-model Mixture-of-Kittens (MoK) benchmark
+workloads. They use mock data and force-balanced routing, not a convergence
+training configuration. Besides Slurm with Pyxis and NVIDIA mlperf-common's
+`bindpcie` script, no launch toolkit is required.
+
+## Workloads
+
+All three recipes use 78 transformer layers (3 dense and 75 MoE), 256 experts,
+hidden size 6144, repeated MTP depth 7, MXFP8 GEMMs and parameter gather, cuDNN DSA, and
+full-iteration CUDA Graphs. Parallelism is TP1/PP4/EP64/configured CP64 with
+expert TP1, on 256 GB300 GPUs across 64 four-GPU nodes. With dynamic context
+parallelism (`dynamic_context_parallel`), CP64 is the largest group: the scheduler
+runs each sample on a CP group no smaller than the smallest power of two that
+keeps each GPU within `max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank` tokens (4,096 at 4K and 128K,
+16,384 at 1M), and it may use a larger group to balance work or to leave no GPU
+idle. At that smallest size, these recipes' fixed-length samples fill all 64 GPUs
+of the CP64 group in every microbatch, so it is the realized CP that the table
+below gives.
+
+The DSA indexer scores keys in MXFP8 with DeepGEMM (`dsa_indexer_precision: mxfp8`,
+`dsa_indexer_scorer_backend: deepgemm`) and selects them with DeepSelect
+(`dsa_indexer_topk_backend: deepselect`). Megatron uses DeepSelect on these BF16
+scores only for top-k calls at least 16,384 keys wide; a call is as wide as the
+longest key span among its rows. At 128K and 1M every call uses DeepSelect. At 4K
+every training call is narrower (realized CP1, at most 4,096 keys), so the cuDNN
+top-k runs in every iteration; only Megatron's pipeline prewarm
+(`pipeline_model_parallel_prewarm`), on one synthetic 262,144-token sequence over the
+configured CP64, uses DeepSelect there. The prewarm runs before the first iteration,
+and Megatron logs its time as part of iteration 1, outside the timing samples
+(iterations 13–32). At 1M
+the full-recompute replay reuses the top-k of the first forward
+(`dsa_indexer_reuse_checkpoint_topk`). MXFP8 scoring selects some keys
+differently from BF16 scoring; it needs its own training evidence before production
+use. Each recipe runs the indexer trained (`dsa_indexer_loss_coeff 1e-2`, the
+default) or frozen (`--variant frozen_indexer`: coefficient 0, so the indexer parameters
+take no gradient and the indexer loss is not computed).
+
+The recipes explicitly enable `muon_split_mla_qkv` together with
+`muon_split_qkv_per_head`. The separate MLA opt-in preserves the benchmark's
+per-head up-projection optimizer behavior on current dev; omitting it would
+orthogonalize those weights as whole matrices.
+
+| Recipe | Valid tokens/sample | Realized CP | GBS | Microbatches/step | Recompute | MoK macro |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
+| [THD 4K](gb300/mxfp8_THD4K_256GPU_TP1PP4EP64CP64_full_cg_mok.yaml) | 3,968 | 1 | 2,048 | 32 | Selective layernorm | 40,960 |
+| [THD 128K](gb300/mxfp8_THD128K_256GPU_TP1PP4EP64CP64_full_cg_mok.yaml) | 126,976 | 32 | 64 | 32 | Selective layernorm | 40,960 |
+| [THD 1M](gb300/mxfp8_THD1M_256GPU_TP1PP4EP64CP64_full_cg_mok.yaml) | 1,015,808 | 64 | 8 | 8 | Full uniform-1 | 131,072 |
+
+Every step carries 8,126,464 valid global tokens (31,744 per GPU). The pipeline layouts are:
+
+- 4K and 128K: `Et*22|t*24|t*24|t*8m*7L`
+- 1M: `Et*10|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*12|t*8|m*7L`, an interleaved schedule with two
+  virtual stages per PP rank (22/24/20/12 decoder layers per rank) and
+  `no_overlap_p2p_communication`, because full-iteration CUDA Graphs are
+  validated with batched PP send/recv only.
+
+With DSA index sharing every fourth layer, every pipeline stage or virtual stage
+must start at a layer that computes its own top-k, so layouts move in steps of
+four layers. In same-allocation A/B runs on 256 GB300 with these recipes' settings
+and runtime stack (the measured runs described under
+[Validation scope](#validation-scope)), the layouts above cut the median step time by 8.2% (4K), 3.7% (128K) and 13.7% (1M)
+against the previous `Et*18|t*24|t*24|t*12m*7L` (4K, 128K) and
+`Et*22|t*24|t*24|t*8m*7L` (1M). MoK's minibatch size is 4096. 4K and 128K share one
+layout; 1M differs in layout, recompute policy and schedule, so the cases are not a
+controlled context-length comparison.
+
+The fixed-length mock samples produce a fixed realized dynamic-CP schedule.
+`cuda_graph_static_dynamic_cp` allows full-iteration capture of that schedule;
+these recipes do not establish support for arbitrary changing dynamic-CP
+shapes under one captured graph.
+
+Each recipe runs 32 iterations: iterations 1–3 warm up, iteration 4 captures,
+iterations 5–12 warm up replay, and iterations 13–32 are the 20 timing samples.
+

+arguments and environment without starting distributed training:

+```bash

+export GLM52_DEEPSELECT=/absolute/path/to/deps-deepselect
+export GLM52_DEEPGEMM=/absolute/path/to/deps-deepgemm

+
+A dry-run is a command audit, not runtime or dependency qualification. Use the
+4K or 1M filename to render the other workloads, and add `--variant frozen_indexer`
+to render the frozen indexer.
+
+The steps below use Slurm with Pyxis, as the measured runs did. Work from the
+Megatron-LM root, on a filesystem that every node mounts, in a clean shell.
+`srun` forwards the shell's environment into every rank, but values that the
+image or enroot's configuration set take precedence: the `environ.d` files and
+`hooks.d` scripts in the cluster's enroot directory (by default `/etc/enroot`)
+and in your own `${ENROOT_CONFIG_PATH:-$HOME/.config/enroot}`, which enroot
+applies even though the container does not mount `$HOME`. Enroot's PyTorch
+hook, for example, sets `MASTER_ADDR` and `MASTER_PORT`, so step 1 exports the
+rendezvous as `GLM52_MASTER_ADDR` and `GLM52_MASTER_PORT`. The recipes and
+`srun_rank.sh` set the NCCL, CUDA, PyTorch, Transformer Engine and OpenMP
+variables they need, so export no other `NCCL_*`, `CUDA_*`, `TORCH_*`, `NVTE_*`
+or `OMP_*` variables from the shell, and set none in your own enroot
+`environ.d` or `hooks.d`.
+
+Allocate 64 nodes exclusively as four 16-node segments, each inside one NVL72
+domain, on a partition and QoS that admit 64 exclusive nodes, for example
+`--nodes=64 --ntasks-per-node=4 --gpus-per-node=4 --segment=16 --exclusive
+--time=2:00:00`. On partitions without GPU GRES, leave out `--gpus-per-node`
+here and `--gpus-per-task` in step 2; every step then sees all four GPUs. In the
+measured runs and in the recipe run (both under [Validation scope](#validation-scope)),
+each training run took 11–13.5 minutes at 4K and 128K and 16–17.5 minutes at 1M, and
+logged its first iteration 3.1–4.1 minutes after it started. Steps 1 and 2 take 1–2
+minutes, so two hours cover all six runs (the recipe run, which ran all six in one
+job, took 1 hour 23 minutes) and one hour covers one context length's two runs, with
+the JIT caches deleted after the job (see step 3). Keep the four variables above set
+and define:
+
+```bash
+export GLM52_RECIPE=examples/moe_recipes/glm5_2/gb300/mxfp8_THD128K_256GPU_TP1PP4EP64CP64_full_cg_mok.yaml
+# Logs and per-rank JIT caches, on a filesystem that every node mounts and that permits exec.
+export GLM52_RUN_DIR=/absolute/path/to/run-directory
+export GLM52_BINDPCIE=/absolute/path/to/bindpcie  # executable, see step 3
+mkdir -p "${GLM52_RUN_DIR}" "${DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR}"
+CPUS_PER_TASK=31  # a quarter of the node's schedulable cores (31 on the measured nodes)
+# Mount each filesystem that holds the paths above (the Megatron root, the three trees,
+# DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR, GLM52_RUN_DIR and bindpcie) at the same path. The measured runs, whose paths
+# were under /scratch, mounted /lustre:/lustre,/scratch:/scratch. $HOME is not mounted.
+CONTAINER=(--container-image=/absolute/path/to/glm52.sqsh
+           --container-mounts=/absolute/path/to/filesystem:/absolute/path/to/filesystem
+           --container-workdir="${PWD}" --no-container-mount-home)
